newsitem.title: UK: Baseball cap supplants top hat in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Baseball cap supplants top hat in Britain.

text.p: The top hat has bowed to the baseball cap in Britain.
The last major manufacturer of the elegant hats that adorned gentlemen in the Royal enclosure at Ascot races is to close, a victim of changing fashions.
"It is the end of an era," said Mark Billing, chief exceutive of Christy of Stockport which has been making hats for the gentry since 1773.
The company had a brief boost in popularity when Hugh Grant wore one of their top hats in the British hit film "Four Weddings and a Funeral".
But the respite proved short-lived. "Formal hat wearing among men is declining rapidly. All the growth is in the youth market with baseball caps," Billing told the London Times on Saturday.
Christy also made the homburgs favoured by British wartime leader Winston Churchill as well as the trilbies sported by Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev.
